title: agent-workflow/v1
description: Authored surface for a declarative agent workflow: a flat sequence of steps with typed outputs, enum routing, and terminal emits. This schema validates the file format only; a workflow compiler performs the deeper checks (reference resolution, route exclusivity, permission ceilings).

on.description: Trigger. Keys and shapes follow the forge/channel event vocabulary.

permissions.description: Ceiling for the credential minted for the run. Agent loadouts must fit under it; they are never declared here.

requires.description: Preconditions verified before the first step. Governance names an org-layer git-forge-governance policy; forge lists workflow-specific observable preconditions.

ref.description: A typed reference to a prior step output or trigger field. References are typed value plumbing, not string templating.

outputSchema.description: A closed JSON Schema for a step or workflow output, inline or as a relative file path (which may point outside the workflows directory, e.g. ../spec/work-graph.v1.schema.json). Inlined and digested identically at bake.

run.description: Deterministic operation: a command that prints JSON conforming to the step's output schema.

agent.description: Agent id from the resolved catalog. The agent's loadout — tools, MCP servers, subagents — is defined on the agent, never here.

uses.description: Reference to a published workflow or task, pinned by digest.

with.description: Named inputs for the step: prior step outputs or trigger fields, passed by typed reference. The handoff is contract, not prose — an agent step receives these as its input artifacts.

if.description: Enum equality over a declared prior output: steps.<id>.output.<pointer> == '<value>'. No other expression forms.

emit.description: Ends the run with the workflow output built from literals and typed references.

runs-on.description: Execution backend: a literal, or a reference to a prior decision step's finite enum, which expands per enum value at bake.

posts-to.description: Forge location where the runtime posts this step's output artifact. Posting is the runtime's write, not the agent's — a read-only agent's output still lands on the pull request.
